record: public index of first-party Dota 2 client evidence held privately outside this repository
why_this_file_exists: Raw client captures are load-bearing evidence for this project and are also personally identifying: they show the operator's Steam persona, a friend's display name, avatars, the friend leaderboard and account point totals. None of that is evidence for anything this repository claims. So the raw bytes stay in a private archive and the public repository publishes the sha256 of each original plus a transcription of only the facts the project actually uses. The hash is a commitment: it pins exactly which bytes were read, so a later reviewer can be handed the private file and verify it is the one that was transcribed, without the image ever being published.
private_archive_layout: <private evidence root>/ti2026/{pre_event,post_event,fantasy}/ plus manifest.private.json. The absolute location is deliberately not recorded here; it is an operator-local path.
repository_local_ingress: evidence_local/ is git-ignored and exists as a staging area for new private captures before they are moved to the private archive. Nothing in it is ever committed.
trust_boundary: Transcription from image to text is done by human-reviewed reading, not by runtime OCR. The hash proves the image has not changed since it was read; it does not prove the reading was correct. Any future change to an image invalidates its record until it is re-read.

main_event_prediction_settlement.track: Main Event bracket predictions (client tab: International Invitational)
main_event_prediction_settlement.official_points_basis: This capture frames the bracket page. It directly shows the 8/14 count for this track, the 6/16 count for the group track, and a settlement mark on every one of the 14 nodes; it does not include the client's settlement summary modal, so no points figure appears anywhere in this frame. The points figure is proved separately and directly by ti2026-ev-006, the settlement summary capture, and independently by deterministic recomputation against entry 8 of the committed 15-entry Main Event scoring vector in data/ti2026/inputs/prediction_questions.json. This record is unchanged in substance and remains valid; it is complemented by ev-006, not corrected by it. See INC-16, now closed.
main_event_prediction_settlement.coverage_basis: the whole 3840x2160 frame was re-examined at native resolution in six tiles during the 2026-08-24 archival correction; the file is a single-frame PNG with no alpha and no hidden frame.
main_event_prediction_settlement.per_node_credit_basis: the capture renders the full 14-node bracket with the operator's submitted pick highlighted at every node and marked by the client with a green check or a red cross. Node identity is established by matching each rendered block against the predicted_matchup recorded in the frozen pre-event artifact, which agrees at all 14 nodes.
main_event_prediction_settlement.display_semantics: the client renders the operator's PREDICTED path at every node, not the realized participants. Downstream blocks therefore show teams that did not play there. The check/cross mark is settlement against the realized node winner, which is why a pick can be marked wrong at a node its team never reached.

group_stage_prediction_settlement.note: recorded for completeness; the group slate is a separate tracked production artifact. Its pre-event expectation was 5.249 correct.

settlement_provenance.claim: TI2026 Main Event settlement is 8 correct / 6 incorrect / 4320 points

inputs: the committed official scoring vector in data/ti2026/inputs/prediction_questions.json

settlement_provenance.agreement: all three agree on 8 correct / 6 incorrect / 4320 points
settlement_provenance.independence_note: A and B are separate client views captured at different moments; C uses no image at all. The evaluator fails closed on any disagreement, so the agreement is enforced rather than observed.
settlement_provenance.status: dual first-party plus deterministic provenance established

legacy_identity_exposure.what: a legacy display-name exposure in frozen pre-event Fantasy state files, published before the post-event archival began
legacy_identity_exposure.decision: preserve history; do not rewrite it
rationale: the exposure already exists in published Git history
rewriting history would break published commit identities and the reproduction they anchor
a rewrite could not recall existing clones, forks or caches in any case
the value is a display nickname, not a datum any conclusion depends on
forward controls that stop it spreading are the effective remedy here
legacy_identity_exposure.forward_control: a test fails if any NEW tracked file carries the name, and fails again if the register of affected files goes stale
legacy_identity_exposure.if_removal_is_later_requested: if the affected person explicitly asks for stronger removal, handle it as a separate privacy and history-rewrite operation, not as part of TI2026 scientific archival work. It is deliberately not performed here.

fantasy_settlement_provenance.claim: the official Fantasy period settlement for two accounts across both TI2026 periods
fantasy_settlement_provenance.why_only_one: an official Fantasy score cannot be recomputed from any source this project holds: madstone, watchers_taken and lotuses_grabbed are unobservable in public match data. The bracket settlement's three-way agreement has no counterpart here.
fantasy_settlement_provenance.corroboration_available: within-frame only: each frame's emblem rows sum to its role score and its role scores sum to its displayed total, both within display rounding. Enforced in code.
